page.layout: One printed page. Title block centred at the top: a small "IN" line, then the title in large capitals and italic, then the author's name and description in centred lines. Below, a verse poem of 31 lines in the main column, opened by a large woodcut initial E. Page number "2" printed at the foot, after a row of three dots.

main_text.head: I N HISTORIAM PHILIPPICO-FRISICAM CLARISSIMI, AMPLISSIMIQUE VIRI D. PIERI WINSEMI, I. C. & Historio-graphi Frisiorum integerrimi, ac Eloquentiæ & Historiarum Professoris Celeberrimi; Amici & Collegæ quondam intimi ac desideratissimi.
main_text.l: ERGONE PIERIDES meritis nec præmia constant?
Nec sua Musarum cultori, & honesta Professo
Nomina sunt clari concessa brabeia laboris?
Ergonè post rigido consumtas frigore noctes
Egelidas, lucemque datam melioribus actis,
Non licuit superesse sibi, superesse suorum
Effectis operum, dignosque hinc carpere fructus?
Sed fuit in fatis, ut quem diversa decerêt
Sæcula nosse suum, vel qui, si commoda nostra
Spectassèt, si PIERIDUM juga sacra sororum
Difficilis Natura gradus servare secundos
Curasset, multos tempus traxisse per annos
Debuerat, Pylio longè dignissimus ævo;
Hunc (veniam fasso da numen) magna gerentem,
Complexumque suâ præclaros mente labores,
Ultrà quos dederat, cunctisque sacraverat ævis,
In medio rerum cursu, Mors sæva Lycæis
Eriperet nostris, ac funere mergeret atro?
Exueretque citum moribundæ carcere molis
Invida vis fati? Quem nunc, heu! squallida gestans,
Oraque, & incomptos jaciens Academia crines,
Luget; & expresso lachrymarum fonte, Patrono
Orba suo, fugiens oculis solatia, questus
Concoquit intempesta suos, gemitusque per auras
Nequidquam evanidas fundit, concussa recenti
Vulnere; cujus agit nunc, præstans ante, profundum
Justitium densis Facundia mersa pruinis.
Quid quod sistra silent præcocis conscia fati?
Et tripodes, & muta chelys, & marcida laurus
Squallent? nec Cyrrhæ cortina remugit ab antro?
Claraque ob abruptam cessant oracula vocem?

page.notes: The title block is set in mixed roman, italic and small capitals; the initial E is a large woodcut letter joined to "RGONE" (small capitals, rendered ERGONE). The verse lines are printed as separate lines and are given as <l>. Doubtful readings: "decerêt", "Spectassèt" and "Hunc (veniam fasso da numen)" are as printed in the scan; the letters are not fully certain. The three dots before the page number are an ornament, not text.
